draft.title: Land reform
card: Before 1949, much of China's farmland was owned by landlords. Many peasants rented land and paid a large share of their crop as rent.
After the Communist victory, the new government took land from landlords and divided it among peasants. The Agrarian Reform Law of 1950 set out the process.
Peasants were encouraged to hold public meetings against landlords. Many landlords were beaten, and many were killed.
Land reform gave the Communist Party strong support among poor peasants. It also broke the power of the landlord class in the villages.
draft.remember: Land moved from landlords to peasants, and violence helped end landlord power.

a.q: Why did land reform help the Communist Party win support in the villages?
opts: It gave land to poor peasants who had rented it
It let landlords keep their land and pay lower taxes
It ended all farming by individual families at once
It gave peasants a vote for the national leader
a.why: Poor peasants who had paid heavy rent now held land of their own, so they backed the party. Letting landlords keep land would not have won peasant support.
a.clue: Think about who received the land.

b.q: In 1951, peasants in a village in Hunan gather to accuse their landlord, Mr Zhao, at a public meeting. What does this show about land reform?
opts: It combined land transfer with public attacks on landlords
It was carried out quietly through payments to landlords
It was led by landlords who chose to give up land
It was a plan to build heavy industry in cities
b.why: Land reform involved meetings where peasants accused landlords, and violence often followed. It was not a quiet, paid or voluntary process. Heavy industry belongs to a different policy.
b.clue: The meeting was a public attack, not a sale.

a.best: It gave land to poor peasants who had rented it

b.best: It combined land transfer with public attacks on landlords

problems.detail: The clue 'The meeting was a public attack, not a sale' gives the answer away. It repeats the key words of the right option ('public attacks') and rules out the payments option, so a student can answer without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts on the card and both answers are sound. The clue for question b gives the answer away by echoing the right option's wording.
